---
title: "Metadynamics of water: from clusters to a surrogate"
subtitle: "Enhanced-sampling MD of water clusters with GFN2-xTB, and a MACE-OFF23 machine-learned potential as the route to accelerated sampling."
---

This is a running results notebook for the project. We validate **GFN2-xTB**
RMSD-metadynamics workflows for water — bias and size sweeps, periodic and free
droplets, and a Diels–Alder reaction — then benchmark a **MACE-OFF23** foundation
potential against xTB, with the longer-term aim of accelerating enhanced sampling.

::: {.callout-note}
## What the RMSD bias is
xTB biases along **Cartesian RMSD** to previously visited structures — not along
any bond or angle. Every CV computed in analysis is a *post-hoc descriptor*, and
`Epot` vs a CV is a **sampled potential-energy landscape from a biased run**, not a
free-energy surface.
:::

## Results at a glance

| # | Study | Headline result |
|---|-------|-----------------|
| 01 | [Bias × size](01-sweep.qmd) | The bias breaks the **weakest** bond — H-bond for clusters, covalent O–H only for a lone molecule; small clusters evaporate. |
| 02 | [PBC & temperature](02-pbc.qmd) | Periodicity **confines** the system (removes evaporation); a large O–O gap is *drift*, not dissociation. |
| 03 | [Droplets](03-droplets.qmd) | **Size suppresses evaporation** — free n=20–50 droplets stay intact; raising `kpush` barely perturbs them (a bias-scaling artifact). |
| 04 | [Diels–Alder](04-diels-alder.qmd) | A real reaction driven and verified: concerted TS, **6.7 kcal/mol** barrier, −394 cm⁻¹ imaginary mode. |
| 05 | [MACE-OFF23](05-mace.qmd) | MACE-OFF23 tracks xTB forces at **r ≈ 0.99**, reproduces droplet MD structure, and scales better (crossover by n≈50). |
| 06 | [kpush scaling](06-kpush.qmd) | The RMSD-bias per-atom force ∝ **kpush/N** — so `kpush` must scale **∝ N**; confirmed on the n=30 droplet. |

## Methods in one paragraph

Gas-phase and periodic **GFN2/GFN1-xTB** metadynamics (built-in RMSD bias),
NVT, 0.5 fs timestep; analysis with ASE / NumPy / pandas. Reactions via
`xtb --path` + relaxed scan + Sella saddle optimization. Surrogate benchmarking
with **MACE-OFF23 (small)** as an ASE calculator. All code, data and figures are
in the [repository](https://github.com/tiangroup-uofa/xtb_metadynamics); each
study page links to its detailed `FINDINGS` document.
